html:
SMTO-CMP-0024 — The AI marked this task as finished the wrong way

GUID: 03d84d74-4cbd-4a8c-8e3e-f0f3dc72b89a
Slug: completion-output-status-mismatch
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • This task was meant to end with no written reply, as a finished action. The AI marked it as an answered question instead, so SMTO asked it to correct that label. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait a moment. SMTO has told the AI which label to use, and it normally finishes on its own. Only the finishing label is wrong, so the AI doesn't need to repeat any work to fix it.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, expand the task and check that the changes you asked for are there. This tells you whether the work is actually done, so you don't ask for the same change twice.
  3. If everything is done, you can leave it. If something is missing, send a message asking SMTO to finish only the missing part. Naming only the missing part keeps SMTO from repeating changes that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed with no written summary.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to redo the whole task; the steps it finished are already saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because the frozen terminal output contract is none (action-only, no chat output requested) but the model declared status answered instead of completed.

What this means

  • An action-only frozen output contract is none but the model declares status answered. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • An action-only frozen output contract is none but the model declares status answered.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare terminal_output_contract and suggested_status while preserving the same evidence.

How to fix it

  • Compare terminal_output_contract (none) with the declared status in completion_feedback; the feedback carries suggested_status=completed and the same evidence revalidates under it. The model should resubmit finish_task with status completed and no message; do not re-execute work. On legacy runs without a captured reply policy, the completion.output_contract Agent Check (Enforce requested output contract) controls this rejection.
  • Align the completion status with the verified output contract result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported status matches the accepted action-only contract after evidence validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
